chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Lil Armstrong's band: Louis the Second and Detroit
summary: Lil featured him as Louis the Second, played the Graystone Ballroom in Detroit and wrote arrangements; agents disliked the tiny wife and big husband billing; irregular work and pro rata pay led him to leave.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: She must be nice to work with, Jonah, huh?
She was great. She was great. And we used to play out at Graystone Ballroom in Detroit, and everywhere.
Did Lil play nice piano?
Yeah, I liked her piano playing, you know, for that --
Yeah.
For the band, you know. In that time, you know, it was great. And she was a nice entertainer, you know, out there with her high hat on and things.
Yeah.
She tried to be a Blanch e [Calloway] type.
Yeah.
And she knew her music, because she wrote some pretty nice things there and we enjoyed it, you know.
Some arrangements?
Yeah. Sure.
No kidding.
Yeah. And we did some things there. I don't think there was too much on it, you know. I don't think the agents and things was too much in favor of going out.
Yeah.
Like that Little Bitty Missus and the great big Louis Armstrong, and they didn't like that. Like they used to put that little bitty Blanche and the big Calloway.
Yeah.
I don't think they enjoyed that too much.
No.
So we played there for awhile. There was Milt on trombone, Milt Robinson, who went out with us with Horace. And Luke was in there. I remember Luke come in on guitar.
Oh, yeah.

Because she wanted four rhythm and four sax with MacRae, and Dick Vance and myself, and Sleepy. So then we travelled around with her. Now, after I get to Detroit, I found out I don't like this, because we're not working regular enough and they're paying you pro rata. So we're not working regular enough, and so we get into the -- I go into John McKinney's Cotton Pickers in Detroit.
